The beetle stands on its six legs and breathes: the acorn shell rises and sinks slightly, the horn bobs a little.
The beetle walks forward on its six legs with a steady scuttling gait, the shell rocking slightly.
The beetle lowers its head and horn close to the ground, crouches and braces its legs, then holds that ready-to-push pose.
The beetle thrusts its head and horn forward hard in a strong pushing shove, then pulls back to standing.
The beetle recoils backward, its shell jolting, then settles back on its legs.
The beetle tips over onto its back, its legs wriggle in the air and then stop moving.
The weasel stands on its hind legs and breathes, its tail swishing slowly side to side and the cloak edge swaying a little.
The weasel scurries forward quickly on its hind legs, low and sneaky, tail streaming behind.
The weasel crouches low and pulls its hooded cloak tightly around itself, eyes narrowing, and holds that crouch.
The weasel springs forward and slashes down with both front claws in one quick swipe, then lands back in its stance.
The weasel flinches backward, its head snapping back, then recovers.
The weasel staggers, falls forward onto the ground and lies still with its cloak draped over it.
The little toadstool breathes slowly: its body squashes down slightly and stretches back up, the cap bobbing.
The little toadstool waddles forward on its stubby feet, hopping slightly with each step.
The toadstool puffs itself up: the body swells rounder and taller, the cap lifts and trembles, cheeks puffed out, holding its breath.
The toadstool squashes down flat and then jerks back up with its cap tossed back and its mouth wide open, then settles.
The toadstool squashes and leans back as if struck, then pops back upright.
The toadstool wilts: it shrinks down and topples sideways, the cap drooping onto the ground.
The squirrel stands upright and breathes, its big tail swaying gently and its ears twitching, the pinecone held in its right paw.
The squirrel hops forward in small bounces on its hind legs, tail bouncing behind it.
The squirrel leans back and pulls its right arm far back behind its head, holding the pinecone ready to throw, and holds that pose.
The squirrel swings its right arm over its head and forward in a fast overhand throw, the arm follows through down in front, then it straightens up.
The squirrel flinches back with its tail puffing up, then recovers.
The squirrel staggers, falls onto its back with its tail flopping down and lies still.
The huge toadstool king breathes slowly: the big body squashes slightly and stretches back up, the cap bobbing, beard twitching.
The toadstool king waddles forward heavily on stubby feet, the big cap swaying with each step.
The toadstool king puffs up its cheeks and leans back, its cap lifting and trembling, and holds the breath.
The toadstool king leans forward sharply and shakes its big cap down toward the front, then straightens up.
The toadstool king recoils backward, the cap wobbling, then settles.
The toadstool king sags, slumps down and topples forward, the big cap crashing onto the ground.
The toadstool king squats down low, squashing its body and bending its stubby legs, getting ready to jump, and holds that squat.
The toadstool king jumps straight up off the ground, then drops down heavily and lands with its body squashed flat, then straightens.
